clue.text: Session intended to raise the spirits

definitions.text: Session intended to raise the spirits

parts.words: Session intended to raise the spirits
parts.note: not a party meant to cheer people up but a sitting at which the dead are called up

explanation.surface: A get-together meant to lift everyone's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where a medium tries to contact the dead is a sitting meant to summon ghosts, the spirits of the clue.

clue.text: Small girl embracing friend of composer

indicators.note: the small girl wraps her arms round the friend, so those letters hold the friend's letters inside

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a chum is a friend

explanation.surface: A little girl hugs a pal of some composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer of songs and piano music.

clue.text: Opposed to a makeweight

parts.note: to make money is to gain it
ST is short for stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a small extra added to balance the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makeweight' looks like one word for a small extra, but it splits into 'make' and 'weight'. A stone (ST) is 14 pounds, an old British unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in opposition to something is to stand contrary to it.

clue.text: Firm remain dubious about money for worker

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the money, holding it inside
something dubious is uncertain or suspect, so the letters of the word beside it are reshuffled

parts.note: L stands for pound (libra), the British unit of money

explanation.surface: A company stays uncertain about paying a wage to a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' turns REMAIN into AMINER, and 'about' sets L inside it after the A, giving ALMINER after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitman who digs underground is a kind of manual labourer.

clue.text: Sport's league ends up being overbearing

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the outer letters carry a word between them
the ends of the word league are its first and last letters

parts.note: across means over, as in going over to the other side

explanation.surface: A sports league turns out to be domineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overbearing' splits into 'over' and 'bearing': L and E from 'league ends' carry ACROSS between them. 'up being' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A field game played with netted sticks, originally from North America, is a sport.

clue.text: Watches for isle appearing directly

indicators.note: the letters appear in a new form, so the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Timepieces are exchanged for an island right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing' signals the anagram of WATCHES FOR ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling in a straight line from one point to another is the idiom for the shortest, most direct route.

clue.text: Right, speed up and run through again

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: pace means speed

explanation.surface: An instruction to go right, accelerate and repeat the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PACE into ECAP. 'speed up' looks like 'accelerate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise the main points once more is to go over them again.

clue.text: Main retainer?

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a retainer here is something that holds it back, not a servant

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea; a retainer sounds like a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal barrier built to stop waves eroding the shore holds back the ocean.

clue.text: Hesitation many have about smuggled message

indicators.note: the first pieces have the next word about them, holding it inside

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
to run guns or drugs is to smuggle them, so smuggled gives ran

explanation.surface: A lot of people pause over a secret note brought in illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: D (500 in Roman numerals) is the crossword's 'many'; ER and D have RAN placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand in its older sense is a message or mission carried for someone.

clue.text: Order has bearing on English uniformed attendant

parts.note: a commission is an order for a piece of work
an air is a person's manner or bearing

explanation.surface: An instruction is relevant to English, or so it appears.
explanation.walkthrough: A COMMISSIONAIRE is a uniformed doorman at a British hotel, cinema or office.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman in livery who greets visitors at a hotel or theatre is a uniformed attendant.

clue.text: Receive information locally, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for locally is spoken and heard as the entry

parts.note: hereabout means in this area, locally

explanation.surface: Getting the local news by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something from others is to be told news of it.

clue.text: Taken to be presiding officer

parts.note: a seat that is taken, and the title of the person who runs a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The person who runs a meeting is named after the seat they occupy, which is 'taken' when someone sits in it.

clue.text: Note Greek character's return is the least amount

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: return means the letter is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician notes that a Greek personality's comeback is tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns MU into UM.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest possible quantity is the lowest amount allowed.

clue.text: Say why it's no longer straightforward

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer
plain means simple, straightforward

explanation.surface: Asking someone to justify why matters have become complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To give reasons for something is to make it clear to another person.

clue.text: Unacceptable idea I abandoned

indicators.note: the letter I is dropped, abandoned by the word for idea

parts.note: a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: A self-centred plan was given up as out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The I comes from the clue's own 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not allowed or not acceptable is said to be outside what is proper, a colloquial British phrase.

clue.text: Way to control German force in battle

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: the German and the force are placed inside the word for control

parts.note: to rule is to control
g is the symbol for the force of gravity, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A way of directing German troops during a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard fight or conflict is a battle.

clue.text: Acts of charity sound effective

parts.note: sound means solid and reliable, so good
a remedy that is effective works

explanation.surface: Charitable acts sound like they get results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a homophone signal but is an adjective meaning reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable deeds done to help others are a religious idiom for kindness.

clue.text: Failing of journalist briefly gone over

parts.note: a failing is a flaw, a defect
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter's shortcoming is quickly passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has switched to the enemy side has changed sides, deserted.

clue.text: Done on purpose to expose general survey

parts.note: something finished is over, done
a view is an aim or purpose, as in 'with a view to'

explanation.surface: Something done deliberately to reveal a broad study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'to expose' only link the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad summary of a subject is a general look at it.

clue.text: Get up and go round vol-cane in the Far Fast

indicators.note: the word for energy goes round the volcano, holding it inside

parts.note: vim means energy, get up and go
Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Energetic travel round a volcano somewhere in eastern Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: VIM splits as VI and M around ETNA. 'Get up and go' looks like instructions but is a noun meaning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The country on the eastern side of the Indochinese peninsula lies in East Asia.

clue.text: Number of times look for Daisy

parts.note: O is nought, a number
X is the multiplication sign, read 'times'
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Someone counts how often they glanced at a woman called Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' is capitalised to look like a name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye is a large white wild daisy of meadows.

clue.text: Translated piece of French funeral ode

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: de is French for 'of'

explanation.surface: A French work for a funeral rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' rearranges PIECE as EPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicede is a mourning poem or elegy sung at burial.

clue.text: Save a quarter on extras

parts.note: to spare money is to save it
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Putting aside twenty-five cents for additional items.
explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points are the 'quarters', so S is a quarter; 'on' puts it after in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare parts kept in reserve are extra items.

clue.text: Doggedly continue with burden

definitions.meaning: to keep going in spite of difficulty
to weigh upon someone, impose on them

explanation.surface: Keep going with a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to persist resolutely and to force something on someone as a weight.

clue.text: We're told to cut very fine

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with sheep

explanation.surface: Being told to cut something very delicately.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is extremely thin and almost transparent.

clue.text: Not a high class of building?

definitions.text: Not a high class of building?

parts.words: Not a high class of building
parts.note: a type of building that is not tall, rather than not posh

explanation.walkthrough: 'high class' reads as upmarket, but 'class' is a category of building and 'high' its height.
explanation.definitionFit: A block with few storeys is a squat type of construction.

clue.text: Mountains in Iran get steeper

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the clue's words Iran get

explanation.surface: Peaks in Iran become more sheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steeper' only completes the picture of the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of peaks is called a mountain range.

clue.text: Seriously injured trainee's out of the navy

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so the letters are put out of shape

parts.note: the possessive 's supplies an S, giving trainees

explanation.surface: A recruit badly hurt has been discharged from the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seriously injured' looks like one phrase, but 'Seriously' is the definition and 'injured' rearranges TRAINEES with N.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sincerely and in good faith is doing it in a grave, determined way.

clue.text: Part of royal collection to-eated in the West Country

parts.note: some means a part of
R stands for royal, as in Royal Navy
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: A piece of the royal collection is housed in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; SOMERSET is one of its counties.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county lies in the south-west region.

clue.text: Sailor's to serve port

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor
to tend is to serve or look after

explanation.surface: A sailor is about to serve some port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian coastal ferry harbour.
